messages:
raj: Heads-up — saw a spike in preemptions this morning in us-west-2 on our p4d-like family. Cost looked good but eviction rate hit ~18% over 2h. Thinking we should revisit diversification + fast-checkpoint strategy.
sarah: Ugh. Where exactly is the contention? specific AZ or instance type?
mike: Looks like AZ a and c, instance type families g5 and p4-like. p4-like had the best perf/cost but highest reclaim.
lin: We should avoid single-family binpacking for latency-sensitive inference pools. Spread across 3 families and use size-aware packing. That reduces correlated evictions.
raj: Agreed. Also consider mixing persistent reserved nodes for a baseline and spot for burst. For Dedicated vs Spot mixing: keep enough reserved to satisfy p99 that needs <50ms.
sarah: For the spot side, can we enable instance-handoff so jobs move to lower perf GPUs when preempted instead of fully failing? i.e., fallback to cheaper a100v3/8 -> then scale-down batch size.
mike: Yes, we can route to compatible model variants. Runtime supports warm-cache migration but we need checkpointing to avoid losing KV cache. Need quick lightweight checkpoint save every N tokens.
lin: Implementation idea: on SIGTERM preemption hook upload lightweight KV snapshot to S3 (or EFS for private customers) with background async uploader. Keep snapshot frequency ~30s for long-running chat sessions. If preemption notice only 2 minutes, we can drain and restore.
sarah: Quick config snippet I used in staging: 
```
preemption:
  handler: checkpoint-uploader
  freq_secs: 30
  upload_target: s3://redwood-spot-kv
fallbacks:
  families: [g5, a100, t4]
  prefer_low_latency: true
  cool_down_secs: 120
```
raj: Nice. Also add eviction-sensitivity weight for binpack: prefer smaller pods on higher-eviction families so we can reschedule faster.
mike: On cost modeling — remember hourly price vs throughput delta: g5 cheaper but ~1.25x latency vs p4-like for long contexts. For transient workloads, cheaper family wins; for steady low-latency requests, reserve the faster family.
ops-bot: Alert: autoscaler scaled spot-pool-usw2 from 120 -> 80 due to reclaim events at 07:14 UTC.
lin: We should also update autoscaler policy: max-binpack-skew=0.15, prefer-family-spread=true, and enable preemptive rebalancer to proactively move state off nodes predicted to reclaim.
sarah: One more ops tweak — add cooldown on scale-in so we don't thrash when a handful of nodes get reclaimed. 300s seems fine.
raj: OK action items: 1) deploy the checkpoint-uploader hook to canary pool (mike), 2) roll autoscaler policy changes to staging (lin), 3) run cost/perf sim for 3 family mixes and report (sarah). I'll track in the infra board.
mike: On it, will push PR with handler + docs.
lin: I'll schedule a short postmortem if reclaim rate stays >10% next 24h.
deploy-bot: Scheduled rollout: checkpoint-uploader v0.1 -> canary (eng-infra) at 08:40 UTC.
raj: Thanks — let's reconvene after the canary metrics. :thumbsup:
